title: Property Valuation Infrastructure and the Implementation of Zimbabwe's Wealth Tax
content: Zimbabwe’s proposed Wealth Tax on high-value residential property has the potential to broaden the tax base, mobilise revenue from accumulated property wealth and contribute to a more equitable distribution of wealth. However, the tax is yet to be implemented, and its effectiveness will depend on the property valuation infrastructure available to support its administration. This paper examines whether Zimbabwe’s existing property information and valuation arrangements provide an adequate foundation for Wealth Tax administration. Drawing on literature and documentary evidence and using the Philippines and Cayman Islands as comparative cases, the paper identifies the information, valuation and institutional requirements for a workable property-based tax. Results indicate that property identification, ownership records, cadastral information, property characteristics, transaction data and valuation processes need to operate as an integrated system. The paper proposes an integrated national property valuation information system that connects these components while retaining the statutory roles of existing institutions.
